court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Madras in FCOP No.215 of 1997
case_name: A. Viswanathan vs G. Lakshmi @ Seetha
facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married in 1992. The husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty under Section 13(1) (i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The Family Court dismissed the petition holding that the respondent has not treated the petitioner with cruelty and rejected the appellant's prayer to dissolve the marriage.

legal_principles.principle: Condonation means forgiveness of the matrimonial offence and the restoration of offending spouse to the same position as he or she occupied before the offence was committed.
legal_principles.held: To constitute condonation, there must be, therefore, two things: forgiveness and restoration.
cited_cases: Dr. N.G. Dastane vs. Mrs. S. Dastane, (1975) 2 SCC 326
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — in determining whether a spouse has condoned the other's cruelty

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty, generally, does not consist of a single, isolated act but consists in most cases of a series of acts spread over a period of time.
